newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST - Australian Business News - Feb 5.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST - Australian Business News - Feb 5.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

According to the latest Bureau of Statistics figures released yesterday, unexpectedly weak retail sales figures - retail sales slumped one percent in seasonally adjusted terms in December - could drive the economy into reverse. Analysts predict the fall in consumer spending could produce non-existent or negative GDP growth when the December quarter national accounts figures are released on March 5. Page 1.

George Palmer QC, acting for new trustees who are seeking to recover more than A$600 million in damages for unit holders, told the Victorian Supreme Court yesterday that advertisements for a major campaign for Estate Mortgage were approved by trustees Burns Philp Trustee Co in 1989 during a major liquidity crisis affecting the trusts. Page 3.

Following an internal review, initiated by Telstra chief executive Frank Blount, the national telecommunications carrier is moving to tighten management controls in its fast-growing mobile telephony business. The review is understood to have centred on marketing and other commercial arrangements entered into by Telstra senior executives. Page 4.

David Jones chairman Dick Warburton revealed yesterday that thanks to substantial improvement in second quarter sales the upmarket retailer had cleared stock faster than expected and restricted its fall in revenue to just one percent to A$72.6 million for the 26 weeks to January 25. Page 19.

Following an opening of the books for Wagga Wagga City Council's natural gas business, which has revealed new financial details indicating that energy utility AGL could undercut the operation to the point of making it barely profitable, potential bidders have softened their interest in the A$20 million-A$30 million Wagga Wagga operation. Page 19.

South African conglomerate Barlow Ltd has revealed it aims to set a target of hauling retail paint supplier Taubmans, which it acquired for A$40 million in October last year after Wattyl Ltd's bid for the business was blocked by the Australian Competitionand Consumer Commission, back into profit by 1998. Page 19.
THE AUSTRALIAN

Recent interest rates cuts have lead to tentative signs of a recovery in the retail sector after David Jones Ltd reported unusually strong January sales. DJ's sales for the 13 weeks to January were up 0.3 percent to A$472 million, which the company said should have a "marginally positive impact" on its half-year profit. Page 21.

U.S.-based Century Communications has signalled its intention to quit its role in Australia's pay-TV industry and is in discussion with its investment advisers to sell its controlling stake in East Coast Television and 25 percent of its programming joint venture XYZ Entertainment. Page 21.

The Australian Bureau of Agricultural and Resource Economics has predicted record mineral earnings during the next two years, with mining to rise 3.7 percent to just over $A36 billion in 1996/97 followed by a 10.5 percent surge to A$38.8 billion in 1997/9. Page 21.

Senior TCI executive and U.S. cable TV expert Fred Vierra has called for Australia's competing pay-TV companies to merge programming and infrastructure or risk waiting a long time for investment in pay-TV to make a profit. Vierra also warned Australian pay-TV companies they could not expect more than 30 percent market penetration. Page 23.

The Vietnamese Government is studying a proposal by BHP to sell its interest in the Dai Hung mine oilfield to Malaysian petroleum giant, Petronas. It is expected the PetroVietnem will take 19 days to assess BHP's proposal, which includes selling its 43.7 percent stake to Petronas, as well as taking over the operations at Dai Hung. Page 23.

Commonwealth Bank managing director David Murray has indicated the bank is considering a move to the scrutinisation market with a A$340 million issue which it hopes will increase competition within the market as well as reducing costs for the bank. This follows Westpac Banking Corp's move into the market last year with a A$340 million issue. Page 23.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

Speaking at an Australian Securities Commission electronic commerce conference yesterday, Commonwealth Bank managing director David Murray strongly indicated CBA would be moving to copy the cheap funding techniques of its low-cost rivals in an effort to protect its A$29 billion home loan business and offer customers lower home loan rates. Page 25.

David Jones has reported a one percent drop in sales across all stores to A$782.6 million from A$790.3 million in the previous corresponding period but the upmarket retailer's figures were bolstered by clearance sales where David Jones brings in special inventory and offers extensive markdowns. Page 25.

Thanks to Australian households' increasing trend towards debt and willingness to spend considerable amounts on credit cards, the amount of business done on Visa cards - both credit and debit - surged 34 percent for the year ended September 30, rising to A$19.5 billion. Page 27.

George Palmer QC, representing trustees acting for 45,000 Estate Mortgage unitholders, told the Supreme Court yesterday a 1987 advertising campaign describing the now-collapsed Estate Mortgage Trusts as safe, secure and better than banks, was released when 42 percent of Estate's trust loans were in default. Page 27.

The Lowy family's new Australian-listed Westfield America Trust, which controls a portfolio of 22 U.S. shopping centres and floated worth A$402 million last year, has confirmed the continued recovery in U.S. retailing by delivering a cash distribution 3.4 percent above the prospectus forecasts for the period from July to December at 4.24 cents a unit. Page 27.

Speaking at the Australian Cable & Satellite Television conference yesterday, Don Hagans, the chief executive of Austar - Australia's largest regional pay-TV group - called for a rationalisation of the industry to ensure its long-term health is protected. Hagans also said he hoped 1997 would see an end to the bitter feuding between the nation's pay-TV companies. Page 29.
THE AGE

Following a series of detailed briefings with angry institutional investors last month, David Jones chairman Dick Warburton conceded yesterday that the upmarket retailer is suffering a serious decline in sales and profits and must put in place its plans to boost merchandising strategies and refurbish its stores in an effort to reverse the negative trend. Page C1.

Speaking at the Australian Bureau of Agricultural and Resource Economics annual Outlook conference in Canberra yesterday, London economist Giles Keating, the chief economist of CS First Boston, said the world economy can now be driven faster than ever before with low risk of crashing, thanks to a deflationary effects of globalisation and the spread of technology. Page C1.

According to forecasts unveiled at the Australian Bureau of Agricultural and Resource Economics annual Outlook conference in Canberra, the edge on Australia's commodity exporting performance would be diminished this year as low world prices affect the rural sector. Page C2.

While final bids in Australia's first airport privatisations remain confidential, confidential sources say the biggest bids for Melbourne and Brisbane almost certainly exceed A$1.2 billion and could even near A$1.4 billion - sums which are puzzling anlysts because, based on earnings, neither Melbourne nor Brisbane should attract more than A$800 million. Page C3.

A move to "securitise" some of its loan book can be expected soon from the Commonwealth Bank after CBA managing director David Murray revealed yesterday the amount of equity the Reserve Bank requires to be set aside for home loans is probably 14 times greater than the amount of equity the bank really needs. Page C3.

Thanks largely to a four percent increase in department store sales in its portfolio, the Australian-listed Westfield America Trust has delivered a cash distribution of 4.24 cents a unit - a result 3.4 percent above prospectus forecasts for the period from July to December. Page C3.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
